transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Hi, thanks. I’ve gotten so strict about what and how much I eat that I’m barely eating at all, and it’s starting to interfere with my work on job sites.
Do you have a strong desire to be thin or a fear of gaining weight that influences your eating habits?

I definitely have a huge fear of gaining weight; if I even think about eating something like pizza after work, I panic that the scale will jump up and clients will see me looking "bigger" in my overalls. I've been trying to stay "lean and light" because in my head, it just means being in "job shape" to move easily on scaffolding.
Do you think your weight or body shape is normal, or do you see yourself as overweight even when others might not?

I don't see myself as overweight at all; I actually think I'm in perfect "job shape" to move easily around tight stairwells and scaffolding. When people worry about my weight or me fainting, I feel like they're blowing it out of proportion and that I'm just tired from hustling so hard.
Do you believe your fear of gaining weight is related to your job requirements or is it also related to how you feel about your appearance in general, outside of work?

It really started with my job and wanting to stay in "job shape" to easily navigate ladders and tight spaces, especially because I worry about clients seeing me look bigger in my overalls. But now, the panic of seeing that number on the scale go up has become so intense that it's hard to separate from my daily life outside of work, too.
Can you think of any situations where you would feel comfortable gaining a small amount of weight, or do you think gaining any weight at all would be unacceptable to you?

Gaining any weight at all feels completely unacceptable and honestly terrifying to me. I feel like I have to stay at this weight to be in "job shape" so I can move easily around tight stairwells and scaffolding. Even the thought of gaining a little weight triggers intense panic that the scale will jump up and my clients will notice me looking bigger in my work overalls.

Do you believe that your fear of gaining weight is primarily driven by the potential impact on your job performance, or is it also significantly influenced by a desire to achieve a certain body shape or appearance for personal or societal reasons?

It’s really a mix of both. On one hand, I feel like I need to stay "lean and light" to easily navigate scaffolding and tight spaces on the job. But on the other hand, there is a lot of pressure to prove myself in a male-dominated trade, and I get terrified of clients seeing me look "bigger" in my work overalls.

When you think about gaining weight, is your primary concern that it will affect your ability to perform your job safely and efficiently, or is it more about how you will look to others and feel about yourself?

It is really a mix of both. I get a rush of panic picturing the scale going up and my clients noticing me looking "bigger" in my work overalls. But at the same time, I have this strong belief that staying "lean and light" is absolutely necessary for me to move easily around tight stairwells, scaffolding, and ladders on the job.
Can you estimate your current weight, and do you think it's significantly different from what others, such as your doctor or friends, might estimate it to be?

I know I've lost weight because my pants hang off me and I've had to punch extra holes in my tool belt, but I just see it as being in "job shape" for moving around scaffolding. My doctor and parents think my weight is dangerously low and are making a huge deal out of my low blood pressure and fainting. I honestly feel like they're blowing it out of proportion and that I function just fine.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as underweight, even if others are concerned that you're too thin, or do you genuinely believe you look fine or even overweight?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as dangerously underweight at all; I just see someone who is in "job shape" and the right size to move around tight scaffolding. I honestly think my parents and doctors are blowing my weight out of proportion. To me, I look fine and function just fine for the demanding work I do.
Do you think your perception of your body shape and weight is different from how others see you, and if so, how does that affect your eating habits and fear of gaining weight?

Yes, there is a big disconnect; my parents and doctor worry about my weight loss and low blood pressure, but I just see my body as being in "job shape" to navigate scaffolding. This drives me to strictly limit what I eat, like skipping lunch for black coffee in my van, because the thought of gaining weight and looking "bigger" in my work overalls causes me pure panic.
Do you think you would still have this intense fear of gaining weight if you weren't working in a physically demanding job that requires you to navigate tight spaces?

Honestly, yes, I think I would still have this fear. Even though I tell myself it's just about being in "job shape" to move through tight spaces, the sheer panic I feel when I think about the scale going up or looking "bigger" feels much deeper than just a work requirement.

If you were to switch to a job that didn't require you to be in tight spaces or climb scaffolding, do you think your fear of gaining weight and your strict eating habits would decrease, or would they remain the same?

I think they would probably remain the same, because even though I tell myself it's just about being in "job shape" for work, the fear of losing control runs much deeper. Even if I switched jobs, the intense panic of seeing the scale go up or looking "bigger" would still be there because controlling my eating has become such a rigid habit.

Do you believe that if you were to gain weight and no longer fit into your current work clothes, your worth or identity as a person would be significantly affected, beyond just your ability to perform your job?

Absolutely, my identity is deeply tied to my work and my professional image. Gaining weight and looking "bigger" in my overalls would make me feel like I’ve completely lost control and failed to maintain my "job shape." I would feel like I’ve lost the disciplined image I need to prove myself in a male-dominated trade.

Would you say that your fear of gaining weight is more about maintaining a certain body image that you associate with being competent and professional in your job, or is it strictly about the physical requirements of your job and how weight gain would affect your ability to perform tasks like climbing scaffolding?

It is definitely a mix of both. On the physical side, I feel like I need to stay lean and light to easily climb scaffolding and move around tight stairwells. But there's also a deep anxiety about my image, because I'm terrified of looking "bigger" in my overalls and failing to maintain that disciplined, professional look in a male-dominated trade.

If you were able to achieve your ideal body shape and weight, but still had to wear loose or baggy work clothes that hid your physique, would your fear of gaining weight and strict eating habits decrease, or would they remain the same?

They would definitely remain the same, because even if baggy clothes hid my shape, I would still panic about the actual number on the scale rising. I would also still feel that internal need to be physically "light" and small enough to move easily through tight stairwells and scaffolding on the job.

If you were to achieve a weight where you felt physically capable of performing your job safely and efficiently, but still felt that your body shape or size was not ideal according to your personal standards, would you continue to restrict your eating to try to achieve that ideal body shape?

Yes, I would definitely still feel compelled to restrict my eating because the fear of losing my lean shape is just too intense. The sheer panic of looking "bigger" in my overalls or losing control over my size would completely override any desire to just be physically capable.

If your job no longer required you to wear form-fitting overalls and you could wear loose clothing that didn't reveal your body shape, would your fear of gaining weight and your strict eating habits change?

No, my habits and fears wouldn't change, because loose clothing wouldn't stop me from panicking at the thought of the scale going up. I would still feel this absolute need to stay "lean and light" so I can move easily on ladders and scaffolding. Even if other people couldn't see my body, I would still know my size, and I just can't tolerate gaining weight.

If you were able to maintain your current weight and body shape, but had a medical condition that required you to take medication that would cause a slight weight gain, would you still be as fearful of gaining that weight, or would your focus on maintaining your health override your fear of weight gain?

Even if it were for a medical condition, the fear of gaining weight would absolutely override my focus on health, and I'd be terrified to take the medication. The thought of the scale going up or looking "bigger" in my overalls triggers immediate panic, and I tend to downplay medical concerns anyway because keeping my weight down feels so much more urgent.

If you were to gain weight but still be able to perform your job safely and efficiently without any issues, would your distress about the weight gain be primarily due to how you feel about your appearance, or would it be more about the potential impact on your job performance?

Even if my job performance remained perfect, my distress would still be mostly about my appearance and the scale itself. I would feel absolute panic seeing the number on the scale go up and constantly worry about clients or others noticing I look "bigger" in my work overalls. Although I try to justify my current size as just being in "job shape" for tight spaces, the thought of actually looking larger is what really terrifies me.

If you were to gain weight and still be able to perform your job without any issues, would you be able to accept the weight gain if you didn't have to worry about how you look in your work overalls or to others?

No, even if all those worries about how I look to others were completely gone, the idea of gaining weight would still trigger intense panic. Just seeing the number on the scale go up is terrifying on its own. On top of that, I still have a strong internal belief that I need to stay very light and lean to move easily around scaffolding and tight spaces on my job sites.

If you were able to completely separate your self-worth and identity from your body shape and weight, and only focus on your job performance, would your fear of gaining weight and strict eating habits decrease?

It’s really hard to separate the two because I've deeply linked being "lean and light" with my actual job performance and fitting into tight spaces on site. There's so much pressure to prove myself in a male-dominated trade that looking "bigger" in my overalls feels directly tied to how professional I am. Even if I tried to focus only on performance, the fear of seeing the scale go up or losing that "light" feeling would still make it very hard to let go of my strict habits.
If you were to gain weight but your body shape didn't change, just the number on the scale, would your distress be as significant?

Yes, absolutely. Just seeing the number on the scale go up would cause massive panic and distress for me, because that number is so tied to my sense of control. At the same time, I would still worry about looking "bigger" in my work overalls, so both the scale and my physical size are major triggers.

Would you say that your fear of gaining weight is more closely related to the potential negative impact on your job performance, or is it more about the negative impact on your self-image and how you perceive your body?

It’s really a mix of both. I worry about losing the "lean and light" feeling of being in "job shape" to move easily on scaffolding, but I also have a deep panic about clients noticing I look "bigger" in my work overalls.
If you were to gain weight but could still fit into your current work clothes and perform your job without any issues, would your distress about the weight gain be significantly reduced?

No, my distress wouldn't really be reduced at all because gaining weight would still cause me intense panic. I am absolutely terrified of seeing the actual number on the scale go up, and I would still be constantly scared of looking "bigger" in my overalls. Even if my clothes still fit and I could do my work, that fear of looking larger is just too strong.

If you were to gain weight but still be able to fit into your work clothes and perform your job safely and efficiently, would your fear of gaining weight be significantly reduced if you knew that no one, including yourself, could notice the weight gain?

Even if absolutely nobody else could see it, the fear of gaining weight is so deeply internal that it wouldn't make a difference. Just knowing the scale went up and losing that "lean and light" feeling of being in "job shape" would trigger an intense panic and make me feel like I’ve completely lost control. Because of that rigid need for control, it's really hard for me to imagine ever being okay with any weight gain.
